sources.apa_citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

domains.name: World — Conditions & Possibilities
domains.definition: Engagement with the facticity of being in the world and the practical question of claiming one's place amid conditions and possibilities.

existential_needs.name: Protection / Acceptance
existential_needs.justification_quote: “This demands three things: protection, space and support.—Do I enjoy protection, acceptance, do I feel at home somewhere?”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

existential_needs.name: Space
existential_needs.justification_quote: “This demands three things: protection, space and support… Do I have enough space for being there?”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

existential_needs.name: Support
existential_needs.justification_quote: “This demands three things: protection, space and support.—Where do I find support in my life?”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

existential_needs.name: Acceptance & Endurance (Active part)
existential_needs.justification_quote: “My active part… is to accept the positive sides and to endure the negative sides… To accept means to be ready to occupy the space, to rely on the support and to trust the protection; in short ‘to be there’ and not to flee. To endure means the force to let be whatever is difficult…”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

positive_indicators.justification_quote: “But if I do have these three things, I will be able to feel trust in the world and confidence in myself, maybe even faith in God. The sum of these experiences of trust is the fundamental trust…”
positive_indicators.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

risk_markers_if_unmet.justification_quote: “If this is not the case, the result will be restlessness, insecurity and fear.”
risk_markers_if_unmet.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

coping_reactions.justification_quote: “If this is not the case, psychodynamics takes over the guidance in the form of coping reactions, which are to secure life.”
coping_reactions.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

inclusion_criteria: Statements about feeling safe/unsafe, belonging, room to exist, external supports/barriers.
Narratives of accepting or enduring immutable conditions to take up space in life.
exclusion_criteria: Purely emotional liking of life without reference to safety/space/support (code under FM2).
Identity/values-focused content without conditions of being (code under FM3).

subthemes.name: Claiming a Place
subthemes.justification_quote: “Can I claim my place in this world under the conditions and with the possibilities I have?”
subthemes.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

subthemes.name: Letting-be / Toleration
subthemes.justification_quote: “Man procures himself the space he needs with his ability to tolerate and to accept conditions.”
subthemes.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

domains.name: Life — Relationships & Emotions
domains.primary_question: “I am alive—do I like this fact?”
domains.definition: Relational and emotional engagement that gives depth and value to existence through time, closeness, and communal ties.

existential_needs.name: Relationship
existential_needs.justification_quote: “In order to seize my life, to love it, I need three things: relationship, time and closeness.”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

existential_needs.name: Time
existential_needs.justification_quote: “Do I take time for valuable things, worthy to spend my time for? To take time for something means to give away a part of one’s life while spending it with someone or something.”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

existential_needs.name: Closeness
existential_needs.justification_quote: “Can I feel close and maintain closeness to things, plants, animals and people? Can I admit the closeness of someone else?”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

existential_needs.name: Consent to feeling / being touched
existential_needs.justification_quote: “If life is to make me move freely, my consent to being touched (to feeling) is necessary.”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

positive_indicators.indicator: Harmony with world/self; depth of life; fundamental value
positive_indicators.justification_quote: “If these three conditions are fulfilled, I experience myself as being in harmony with the world and with myself, and I can sense the depth of life… The sum of these experiences… represents our yardstick for anything we might feel to be of worth.”
positive_indicators.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

risk_markers_if_unmet.justification_quote: “If relationships, closeness and time are lacking, longing will arise, then coldness and finally depression.”
risk_markers_if_unmet.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

inclusion_criteria: Accounts of investing time in people/things, seeking closeness, turning toward/away in grief or love.
Descriptions of emotional resonance (being touched) in relationships or activities.
exclusion_criteria: Safety/space/support concerns without relational content (code under FM1).
Identity/ethical self-affirmation without felt relatedness (code under FM3).

subthemes.name: Turning Toward / Engagement
code_examples: Grieving a loss by turning to it
subthemes.justification_quote: “I seize life… when I turn to other people… If I turn to a loss, grief arises.”
subthemes.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

subthemes.name: Pathic Dimension of Life
subthemes.justification_quote: “It has a ‘pathic dimension’… Being alive means to cry and to laugh… The amplitude of emotionality is equal in both directions.”
subthemes.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

domains.name: Person — Uniqueness & Conscience
domains.primary_question: “I am myself—may I be like this?”
domains.definition: Identity, autonomy, and ethical self-affirmation grounded in being seen, treated justly, and appreciated.

existential_needs.name: Attention (being seen; boundaries respected)
existential_needs.justification_quote: “In order to succeed here, it is necessary to have experienced three things: attention, justice and appreciation.—…by whom am I seen? Who considers my uniqueness and respects my boundaries?”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

existential_needs.name: Justice
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

existential_needs.name: Appreciation
existential_needs.justification_quote: “For what am I appreciated—for what can I appreciate myself?”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

existential_needs.name: Saying yes to oneself; encounter and regret
existential_needs.justification_quote: “I also have to say ‘yes to myself.’… Encounter and regret are the two means by which we can live our authenticity without ending up in solitude.”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

positive_indicators.indicator: Authenticity, relief, self-respect; self-esteem as core worth
positive_indicators.justification_quote: “If… these experiences have been made, I will find myself; find my authenticity, my relief and my self-respect… The sum of these experiences builds one’s own worth… the self-esteem.”
positive_indicators.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

risk_markers_if_unmet.justification_quote: “If these experiences are missing, solitude will be the result, hysteria as well as a need to hide behind the shame.”
risk_markers_if_unmet.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

inclusion_criteria: Statements about being seen/respected, boundary-setting, deservingness, right-to-be.
Reflections on authenticity, conscience, regret, or standing by oneself.
exclusion_criteria: Meaning-making and future-directed contribution (code under FM4).
Purely relational warmth/time/closeness without identity concerns (code under FM2).

subthemes.name: Boundarying & Encounter
subthemes.justification_quote: “to look at other people, to encounter them and, at the same time, to demarcate myself and to stand by my own, but to refuse whatever does not correspond to me.”
subthemes.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

domains.name: Meaning — Becoming, Future & Commitment
domains.primary_question: “I am there—for what is it good?”
domains.definition: Orientation toward valuable, realistic possibilities in a broader context, calling for dedication and responsible action.

existential_needs.name: Field of Activity (place to be needed/productive)
existential_needs.justification_quote: “For this, three things are necessary: a field of activity, a structural context and a value to be realized in the future.—is there a place where I feel needed, where I can be productive?”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

existential_needs.name: Structural Context (larger orientation)
existential_needs.justification_quote: “Do I see and experience myself in a larger context that provides structure and orientation to my life?”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

existential_needs.name: Future Value to Realize
existential_needs.justification_quote: “Is there anything that should still be realized in my life?”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

existential_needs.name: Phenomenological Openness (attitude)
existential_needs.justification_quote: “This attitude of openness represents the existential access to meaning in life: ‘What does this hour want from me, how shall I respond?’”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

existential_needs.name: Meaning as most valuable realistic possibility
existential_needs.justification_quote: “[Meaning is] ‘the most valuable, realistic possibility of the given situation, for which I feel I should decide myself.’”
existential_needs.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

positive_indicators.indicator: Dedication, action, sense of fulfillment; religious belief
positive_indicators.justification_quote: “If… these conditions are met, I will be capable of dedication and action and, finally, of my own form of religious belief… adds up to the meaning of life and leads to a sense of fulfillment.”
positive_indicators.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

risk_markers_if_unmet.justification_quote: “If this is not the case, the result will be a feeling of emptiness, frustration, even despair and frequently addiction.”
risk_markers_if_unmet.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

inclusion_criteria: Testimony about contributions, callings, responsibilities, decisions toward valued possibilities.
Situational appraisals of ‘what is asked of me now’ and commitments to future-oriented values.
exclusion_criteria: Identity/entitlement content without future-oriented commitment (code under FM3).

subthemes.name: Answering the Situation’s Call
code_examples: What does this hour want from me?
subthemes.justification_quote: “My active part… is to bring myself into agreement with the situation, to examine whether what I am doing is really a good thing: for others, for myself, for the future, for my environment.”
subthemes.citation: Längle, A. (2011). The Existential Fundamental Motivations Structuring the Motivational Process. In D. A. Leontiev (Ed.), Motivation, Consciousness and Self-Regulation (pp. 27–42). Nova Science Publishers. https://laengle.info/userfile/doc/FM-+-motivation---Leontev-Mosc-2002-2011-publ.pdf

global_coding_notes.note: Use FM1–FM4 as primary domains. Code subthemes only if anchored in verbatim testimony that fits the LM source quotes. When in doubt, prioritize the participant’s expressed question (can I be? do I like life? may I be myself? for what is it good?).
Do not infer content beyond direct quotes supported by the provided sources. Expand this codebook only with additional user-provided academic materials.
